newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon sees Q3 EPS on target, minus charge.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon sees Q3 EPS on target, minus charge.

text.p: Raytheon Co said on Friday that it expects its earnings per share for the third quarter to approximate analysts' expectations before a previously announced special $.09 per share charge to close its Delaware, Ohio, plant.
The First Call estimate for the company's third quarter earnings is $0.89 per share.
Operating income will be down about 15 percent because of delays in awards and contracts at its Raytheon Engineers & Constructors unit and weakness in the appliance sector, the company said.

The company said it expects tax credits for research and development and interest income to offset the shortfall in operating income and strike-related losses at its heavy equipment manufacturing plant in Cedar Rapids, Iowa.
The plant is part of Raytheon Engineers & Constructors, said company spokeswoman Elizabeth Allen.

The strike at Cedar Rapids caused a third quarter operating loss of about $8 million, said company Chief Financial Officer Peter D'Angelo. D'Angelo said the strike has ended and "the operation should return to profitability in the fourth quarter."
Raytheon said operating income for the third quarter 1995 was $354 million.
The company said delays in engineering and construction awards and weakness in the appliance sector will also affect its fourth quarter.
The company said, however, that it expects earnings per share for the year to exceed last year's.
The company reported 1995 operating earnings of $0.90 per share for the fourth quarter and $3.23 for the year.
Raytheon said it will issue its third quarter figures on October 15.
